disputed.rationale: Staff following the procedure would refuse a late dispute from a traveling or hospitalized customer, which the policy allows. The policy outranks the procedure, so the policy clause is the one to keep.

The policy counts 15 business days while the procedure counts 15 days, which ends sooner. Staff following the procedure would work to a stricter deadline than the policy sets, and the policy is the clause to keep.

The policy names the regional manager while the procedure says only management. Staff following the procedure could escalate to a lower level manager, which the policy does not allow, and I decided the general wording widens who can act.

The policy allows one form plus a verified bank reference with branch manager approval and the procedure leaves that out. Staff following the procedure would refuse a signer the policy accepts, and I decided the missing exception makes it a conflict.

The policy allows a hold of up to 7 business days while the bulletin caps it at 7 days, which ends sooner. Staff following the bulletin would release funds earlier than the policy requires, and the policy is the clause to keep.
The procedure covers only commercial accounts and outgoing commercial wires, and it names operations staff for that line. I decided this is a narrower scope stated on purpose, so it is a variation.
The policy allows up to $50 with branch manager approval and the bulletin leaves that out. Staff following the bulletin would refuse a waiver the policy allows, and the policy is the clause to keep.

The policy counts 2 business days while the FAQ counts 2 days, which can end sooner over a weekend. Staff following the FAQ would send acknowledgments on a stricter clock than the policy sets, and the policy is the clause to keep.

One policy limits approval to the branch manager while the other lets any manager approve. Staff following the second could accept an exception from a manager the first does not permit, and I decided the general wording widens who can act.

Both clauses cover the same accounts and branches. Staff following the bulletin would refuse an account that the policy lets a branch manager approve with one form and a bank reference. The policy outranks the bulletin, which only tells the reader which clause to keep.
Both procedures apply to all branches and business lines. Fifteen days of receipt can be shorter than 15 business days, so staff following one could miss the deadline in the other.

Both clauses say who completes the callback on an outgoing wire for all branches and business lines. One limits it to a wire specialist and the other names an operations employee, so an operations employee who is not a wire specialist would be allowed by one clause and barred by the other.

Consumer accounts fall under both procedures, and the second one is not a deliberate narrower variation on this rule. Staff following the first would refuse an account that the second allows with manager approval.

Both clauses cover the same accounts and branches. The policy outranks the procedure, which only tells the reader which clause to keep.
